record.paper_title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
record.original_question: In fully decentralized federated learning, how can personalized-model methods and incentive or mechanism-design schemes be made robust to malicious actors, unreliable labels, unreliable data, and the absence of a trusted central server?

evidence.quote: robustness of such schemes to malicious actors

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a fully decentralized federated learning setting consisting of a finite set of agents $\{1,\dots,N\}$, each holding a local dataset $D_i$ drawn from an agent-specific distribution $\mathcal{P}_i$ on $\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{Y}$. There is no trusted central server: agents communicate only along edges of a (possibly time-varying) graph $G=(V,E)$, and each agent $i$ wishes to learn a personalized model $\theta_i\in\Theta$ that approximately minimizes its local population risk $R_i(\theta_i)=\mathbb{E}_{(x,y)\sim\mathcal{P}_i}[\ell(\theta_i;x,y)]$ while benefiting from collaboration with other agents.

Assume the following adversarial conditions hold simultaneously:
(a) Byzantine agents: an unknown subset $B\subset V$ with $|B|\le \beta N$ may send arbitrary, adaptively chosen messages.
(b) Label noise: for each honest agent $i\notin B$, observed labels are corrupted versions of true labels with unknown agent-dependent noise rate.
(c) Data noise: feature vectors of honest agents may be corrupted by unknown, possibly adversarial perturbations bounded in some norm.
(d) No trusted coordinator: there is no entity that can verify identities, audit data, or aggregate gradients honestly.

Design and analyze:
1. A personalized-model protocol that produces, for every honest agent $i$, a model $\hat\theta_i$ satisfying a provable excess-risk guarantee $R_i(\hat\theta_i)-\inf_{\theta\in\Theta}R_i(\theta)\le \varepsilon(N,|D_i|,\beta,\text{noise})$ that degrades gracefully in the fraction $\beta$ of Byzantine agents and in the label/feature noise levels, under conditions (a)–(d).
2. An incentive or mechanism-design scheme (e.g., a payment/contribution rule or game-theoretic protocol) executed peer-to-peer without a trusted third party, such that truthful participation with honest data and labels is a (dominant-strategy or approximate Bayes–Nash) equilibrium for every honest agent, and such that Byzantine deviations cannot improve their utility by more than a vanishing amount while honest agents retain the personalization guarantee from item 1.

Either construct such a protocol and mechanism with explicit conditions and rigorous guarantees, or prove an impossibility result identifying the precise tradeoffs between $\beta$, the noise levels, the connectivity of $G$, and achievable personalized excess risk.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is a high-level open research direction in federated learning. Partial progress exists on Byzantine-robust decentralized optimization, on personalized federated learning, and on incentive mechanisms separately, but no known work simultaneously resolves robustness to malicious peers, noisy labels, noisy features, and the absence of a trusted server in a fully decentralized personalized setting with rigorous incentive guarantees. The overarching problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
status_evidence.snippet: Survey explicitly lists robustness of personalization and incentive schemes in decentralized FL as open problems.
status_evidence.claim: The combined problem is identified as open in the federated learning research community.

status_evidence.title: Byzantine-Robust Decentralized Learning via Self-Centered Clipping
status_evidence.snippet: Provides Byzantine-robust decentralized SGD but without personalization or incentive mechanisms.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial progress exists on the Byzantine robustness aspect.

status_evidence.title: Incentive Mechanisms for Federated Learning: A Survey
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys incentive designs but notes that decentralized, robust, personalized incentive schemes are largely unaddressed.
status_evidence.claim: Incentive mechanisms in fully decentralized robust personalized FL remain open.
